text:
customer_matt: Hey team — running into a weird streaming issue with the Python SDK 2.4.0. When the token refresh happens mid-stream the client reconnects but the iterator yields a truncated final chunk or duplicated suffix. Request-id: req_20230714_88af.

customer_matt: Minimal repro: start an SSE stream, force a 401 (short token), let SDK refresh, then iterate. Sometimes the final 'DONE' chunk is missing and the iterator ends, other times a tail token is duplicated. Happens consistently for longer responses.

customer_matt: Code snippet (simplified):
```python
async for chunk in client.responses.stream("/v1/generate", json={...}):
    if chunk.type == "delta":
        print(chunk.text, end="")
    elif chunk.type == "final":
        print("<FINAL>")
```

support_claire: Thanks, Matt — sorry you're hitting this. Can you confirm: are you using automatic token refresh via the SDK (Auth callback) or manually re-creating the client? Also which transport (httpx async / requests)?

customer_matt: Using httpx async + SDK built-in token callback (async refresh). I don't manually re-create the client.

sdk_sam: @customer_matt — can you try toggling `streaming.auto_reconnect=False` if available? Curious if the SDK's reconnect code is reusing the iterator state incorrectly. Also which exact model + max_tokens?

customer_matt: Model is open-llama-13b, max_tokens ~1024. I tried setting a lower max_tokens; still repros. I can try that flag, will update.

dev_jamie: Noted. We shipped an SSE reconnection change in 2.4.0 that tries to splice pending KV/state across a reconnection to avoid re-generating prefixes. I wonder if race between heartbeat/final frame handling and the iterator draining logic causes an off-by-one in finalization.

qa_ash: I reproduced locally with a harness: start stream, after ~1s return a 401 from auth endpoint, let SDK refresh, then resume. Observed either: (a) final event never emitted (iterator stops), or (b) last ~8 characters duplicated. Script and logs attached in DM.

infra_bot: backend log snippet for req_20230714_88af:
```
[2024-05-14T16:11:12Z] conn=xyz stream=abc status=200 bytes_sent=1723
[2024-05-14T16:11:12Z] conn=xyz stream=abc client_disconnect (code=RESET) after=0.12s
[2024-05-14T16:11:12Z] stream=abc final_frame_sent=false partial_kv_saved=true
```

support_claire: That backend trace is interesting — final_frame_sent=false but bytes_sent>0. Can infra confirm whether the server thinks it sent the trailing event vs aborted?

infra_bot: Server emitted final event but TCP reset happened during last packet. Server rolled partial_kv to cache to allow resume.

sdk_sam: Sounds like the client-side reconnect logic is racing with the heartbeat/finalization path. If the SDK re-creates the connection and starts consuming from the cached prefix but doesn't flush buffered final event, iterator may conclude without emitting final marker. We're likely not atomically swapping buffers.

eng_olivia: We should treat this as a class of race: (1) token refresh triggers reconnect, (2) server may have already queued final event but connection reset prevents full delivery, (3) SDK resume logic uses cached prefix and current connection but misses the final event if it was still in-flight on the previous socket. Proposed short-term fix: make SDK wait for a short drain window (~50-200ms) on reconnect when a finalization token is expected, or prefer re-creating iterator state instead of reusing on resume. Long-term: server should include an idempotent final marker on resume.

support_claire: For a workaround, could you try (A) disable auto_reconnect so SDK raises on 401 and you re-open a fresh stream, or (B) after a reconnect, call `await stream.aclose()` and create a new stream/iterator?

customer_matt: I tried option A (auto_reconnect off) and then re-opened the stream myself after refresh — that made the final chunk consistently appear. Not ideal but workable for now. Thanks.

sdk_sam: We'll cut a patch to 2.4.x to be more conservative on buffer handoff and to avoid signaling iterator completion until all pending frames are processed. Can you DM me the minimal repro script?

qa_ash: Pushing a test into CI that simulates auth refresh mid-stream with partial TCP reset. Reproducer uses httpx local proxy to drop last packet.

dev_jamie: Adding note: the regression likely came from optimizing for low-latency reconnects; we traded atomicity for speed. We'll revert the aggressive handoff in the patch.

support_claire: Escalation created: INC-7123 (streaming iterator finalization race). Engineering will ship a 2.4.1 patch. For customers: recommended workaround is to explicitly re-create stream/iterator after a token refresh or set auto_reconnect to false.

customer_matt: Patch and workaround sound good. Appreciate the quick triage.

sdk_sam: Thanks, @customer_matt. If you can share the repro I'll prioritize the patch. Also sending you a temporary forked wheel that adds a 150ms drain window on reconnect.

customer_matt: Received the wheel, tested — drain window fixed it for our case. Will keep you posted if anything else crops up. :thumbsup:

support_claire: Marking thread as tracked. If anyone else sees similar symptoms across languages (JS/TS/Go) please report — the root cause is protocol-agnostic (socket-level final packet loss + aggressive client handoff).

eng_olivia: We'll follow up with design doc for a resume-safe framing header so finalization is explicit on resume.

support_claire: Thanks everyone. Closing the customer-facing loop now.
